findings.evidence: Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/Defs.lean:403 `@[simps, instance_reducible] def indexNeg : InvolutiveNeg ι where neg i := P.reflectionPerm i i`; Defs.lean:412 `lemma ne_neg ... letI := P.indexNeg; i ≠ -i` states the `-` form under the same `letI`.
findings.fix: State it as `g.indexEquiv (-i) = -g.indexEquiv i` using both bound `indexNeg` instances (Mathlib writes `RootPairing.ne_neg : i ≠ -i` this way), or rename to `indexEquiv_reflectionPerm_self` if the unfolded form is intended.
findings.issue: `indexEquiv_neg` names the argument `neg` but states the left side as `g.indexEquiv ((P.reflectionPerm i) i)` while the right side uses `-g.indexEquiv i`; the bound `letI := P.indexNeg` is then unused. As a `simp` lemma the key is `RootPairing.reflectionPerm`, so it never fires on the `g.indexEquiv (-i)` form the name advertises.

findings.evidence: EquivInvariance.lean:64-65: `(∃ i, P₂.root i = g.toHom.weightMap m) ↔ m ∈ range P.root`.
findings.fix: State `g.toHom.weightMap m ∈ range P₂.root ↔ m ∈ range P.root` (defeq, so the existing proof and the `exact mem_range_root_weightMap_iff g` uses at lines 140 and 159 still work).
findings.issue: `mem_range_root_weightMap_iff` promises `∈ range`, but the left side is the unfolded `∃ i, P₂.root i = g.toHom.weightMap m` while the right side of the same iff is written `m ∈ range P.root` — the two sides of one statement use different spellings of the same predicate, and the `simp` key is `Exists`.

findings.evidence: Mathlib precedent for an iff whose sides are root equalities: Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/Defs.lean `lemma root_eq_neg_iff : P.root i = - P.root j ↔ i = P.reflectionPerm j j` keeps the `eq`.
findings.fix: Rename to `root_indexEquiv_eq_add_iff` and `root_indexEquiv_eq_sub_iff`, and reorder the binders of the `sub` version to `(k j i)` so they appear in statement order.
findings.issue: `root_indexEquiv_add_iff` and `root_indexEquiv_sub_iff` (line 104) state equalities `root k = root i + root j` but omit `eq`, so the names read as being about `root (indexEquiv (i + j))`. Additionally `root_indexEquiv_sub_iff` binds `(k i j)` while the statement uses them in the order `k`, `j`, `i`.

findings.evidence: Mathlib/Logic/Equiv/Sum.lean:209 `sumEmpty_apply_inl`, Sum.lean:274 `sumCompl_apply_inl`, Logic/Equiv/Set.lean:295 `sumCompl_apply_inl` — the `_apply_inl` form is the standard name for an `Equiv` evaluated at `Sum.inl`.
findings.issue: `geckIndexEquiv_inl` and `geckIndexEquiv_inr` (line 119) are applied-form lemmas for an `Equiv` but omit `apply`, inconsistent with `geckModuleEquiv_apply` at line 133 in the same file.

summary: Names are broadly conventional and no notation is added, but four declarations carry names that do not match the form of the statement: `indexEquiv_neg` writes its left side as `reflectionPerm i i` rather than `-i`, `mem_range_root_weightMap_iff` writes an unfolded existential instead of `∈ range`, the two `root_indexEquiv_*_iff` names drop the `eq` for an equality conclusion, and the `Sum.inl`/`Sum.inr` lemmas omit `apply`.
